newsitem.title: USA: NUTRITION MEDICAL SEES INFANT FORMULA ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: NUTRITION MEDICAL SEES INFANT FORMULA ON TRACK.

text.p: Nutrition Medical Inc said Monday that development of an infant formula remains on track and it expects launch of the product in the 1998 first quarter.

"Our goals for the balance of 1997 remain consistent; we will continue to build our core clinical and retail business while developing new products that will reinforce our presence in the nutrition industry," said William Rush, president and chief executive officer. "Infant formula development remains on track and we expect to ship opening orders in the first quarter of 1998," he said in a news release.

Earlier today, the company reported 1997 second quarter sales of $1.3 million and a net loss of $468,569, or $0.08 a share based on 5.5 million shares outstanding. In the same period last year, sales totaled $381,126 and the net loss amounted to $170,705, or $0.05 on 3.1 million shares outstanding.

Higher sales reflect additional business derived from the acquisition of products from Elan Pharma Inc in January 1997, as well as increases in the company's core retail and clinical lines. The second quarter loss benefited from an insurance reimbursement of $145,000 for legal fees related to two previously settled legal actions.

During the quarter, Nutrition Medical said it added two formulas to its clinical product line: Pro-Peptide For Kids, a diet for children; and Gluco-Pro, its first formula designed specifically for diabetics.

The company said each has been well received and it is encouraged by the level of interest expressed by current and prospective customers. The company said it is adding to its sales force to market the products.
